result.title: DramaVQA: Probing Detailed Understanding of Ultra-Long TV Dramas
result.summary: Despite recent progress in long-form video understanding, current benchmarks mostly focus on short clips or hour-scale videos. This leaves a major gap in evaluating ultra-long video understanding, where videos often last tens of hours. To bridge this gap, we introduce DramaVQA, a large-scale benchmark built upon long-form TV dramas. Containing approximately 20K question-answering (QA) pairs, the scale of DramaVQA exceeds previous long-video datasets, such as Video-MME and LVBench, by an order of magnitude. Our benchmark has two main features that make it stand out from existing datasets. First, we establish a scalable, LLM-assisted annotation pipeline that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking to ensure high data quality. Second, DramaVQA introduces a multi-level time structure; queries are designed across different video lengths, with the hardest questions requiring overall understanding across the entire drama. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges when tested on these very long videos, highlighting the need for agentic AI algorithms capable of managing long-term memory. The project is available at https://github.com/xinyuehuo/DramaVQA

AI.brief_summary: DramaVQA 构建了基于超长电视剧的视频理解基准，约含 2 万条 QA 对，采用 MLLM 辅助生成问题并配合严格人工校验，并设计跨不同时间跨度的多层级问题，评测显示现有 MLLM 在数十小时视频上仍面临明显困难。
AI.relevance_reason: 其多级时间结构与需跨全剧定位证据的问题设置，可作为诊断 VLM 能否保留、筛选视觉证据并维护长期记忆的基准，可供核查与 LVR 中证据获取及推理状态维护的联系。
